definition: SABLE is an XML markup language used to annotate texts for speech synthesis.
details: It defines tags that control how written words, numbers, and sentences are audibly reproduced by a computer. SABLE was developed as an informal joint project between Sun Microsystems, AT&T, Bell Labs, and the University of Edinburgh (the initial letters of each make the word "SABLE") as an initiative to combine three previous speech synthesis markup languages SSML, STML, and JSML. SABLE is used in the Festival Speech Synthesis System. Development on SABLE appears to have stopped in 2010, and it has not reached the status of a formal standard or recommended specification.

explainer.lead: SABLE is a way of adding XML instructions to text so a speech synthesizer can reproduce words, numbers, and sentences as intended. It brought together ideas from three earlier markup languages and is used in the Festival Speech Synthesis System.

tiers.eli5: Reading aloud is easier when someone adds notes, such as how to say a tricky number. SABLE gives a computer those kinds of notes inside a piece of writing. The computer can then use them while turning the writing into speech.
tiers.practitioner: An engineer working with the Festival Speech Synthesis System can use SABLE annotations to control how input text is audibly rendered. Its tags cover written words, numbers, and sentences rather than audio processing itself. Development appears to have stopped in 2010, and SABLE never became a formal standard or recommended specification.
tiers.paperLevel: SABLE is an XML markup language for speech synthesis: annotated text is interpreted by a synthesizer to control the audible rendering of words, numbers, and sentences. It was an informal joint project of Sun Microsystems, AT&T, Bell Labs, and the University of Edinburgh, intended to combine SSML, STML, and JSML. Its limits include the apparent end of development in 2010 and the absence of formal standard or recommended-specification status.

explainer.example: A passage containing a written number can be annotated with SABLE so the synthesizer follows an explicit instruction for its audible rendering, instead of receiving the number as unannotated text.

usedIn.name: Festival Speech Synthesis System
usedIn.detail: Uses SABLE to annotate text for speech synthesis.

usedIn.name: Speech synthesis
usedIn.detail: Provides markup that controls how written words, numbers, and sentences are reproduced audibly.

explainer.intuition: Plain text says what to speak, but it may not say how to speak it. SABLE adds XML annotations that give a synthesizer those missing instructions.
howItWorks: Add SABLE XML tags to the text.
Use the tags to control the audible rendering of words, numbers, and sentences.
Pass the annotated text to a speech synthesizer.
Produce speech guided by both the text and its annotations.
explainer.whyItMatters: SABLE gave developers a common markup approach for controlling speech output, combining three earlier speech synthesis markup languages. Its use in Festival provides a concrete application of that approach.
misconceptions: SABLE is not itself a speech synthesizer; it annotates text that a synthesizer processes.
SABLE is not a formal standard or recommended specification.

diagram.caption: SABLE sits between written text and speech synthesis by adding XML instructions to the input.
